scope: Public-source research only. No outreach, purchases, experiments or claims of physically authenticated material.
novelty_rule: New means no matching exact candidate/use found in the reviewed repository snapshot, round2 proposal inventory or round3 records; not novelty to science or patentability.

deduplication.boundary: Genistein and luteolin are distinct exact screens in the same flavonoid/cystinosis family. Generic autophagy or anti-inflammatory mentions do not establish an exact matched article/use.

priority_changes: AAT mechanistic confidence increases because of independent active/inactive protein and genetic-protease controls. No core-rank promotion is asserted by this domain review.
Sivelestat enters the AAT comparator set; Bis-T-23 enters an exploratory kidney reserve.
FXT-001 remains a secondary benchmark; exact human-organ methods gap persists.
No new entry clears all S-tier gates.

existing_candidate_updates.name: AAT in donor-lung EVLP
existing_candidate_updates.exact_article: Potency-qualified plasma-derived AAT product in a defined warm-EVLP perfusate; recombinant AAT cold-storage study is supporting mechanism, not identical finished product.

independent_unit.unit: independent transplanted mouse graft/recipient; separate paired human donor blocks
independent_unit.count_boundary: New mouse arm-level sample sizes were not recovered reliably. Neither lung sides nor tissue fields are additional donors.

evidence: Independent 2018 study compared active recombinant AAT with a non-inhibitory reactive-center mutant and albumin during cold preservation. PR3/NE-null recipients were also protected; this strengthens protease-specific causality.
The inspected cold-storage regimen used 1 mg/mL AAT, 18h storage and 4h recipient reperfusion. This is separate from the warm human EVLP experiment.
limitations: Exact 2026 human AAT dose/formulation remains unverified; do not import the mouse dose.
Short post-transplant mouse protection is not long-term recipient outcome or proof of complete drug removal.
Label NE potency alone does not establish PR3 neutralization or activity after warm-circuit exposure.
existing_candidate_updates.verdict: RETAIN_CORE_PRIORITY; mechanistic confidence increases; human formulation and durable-graft gates remain.
existing_candidate_updates.decisive_next_proof: Qualify NE and PR3 inhibition in the actual warm perfusate, then compare AAT with physically matched protein/excipient control and an NE-selective comparator. Require postwashout function under recipient-like reperfusion.
existing_candidate_updates.go_rule: AAT supplies persistent useful gas-transfer/compliance benefit at qualified activity and adds value beyond the simpler comparator.
existing_candidate_updates.stop_rule: Stop the differentiated AAT product thesis if physical matching or the simpler comparator explains the useful effect, or if activity is lost before the intended treatment window.
existing_candidate_updates.material_route: Existing manufactured AAT is a public supply route. No lot, stock, warm-circuit compatibility or clinical product identity has been established here.
existing_candidate_updates.model_readiness: Bench activity qualification can precede scarce organs. Local organ access remains unverified; it is separate from scientific merit.
existing_candidate_updates.rights_and_program: Previously identified CSL/UHN context persists. The independent mechanism does not establish new commercial rights.

existing_candidate_updates.name: FXT-001/UAMC-3203 in graft conditioning
existing_candidate_updates.exact_article: Exact UAMC-3203 chemical form and active-moiety concentration must be fixed; free base and hydrochloride are distinct material records.

independent_unit.unit: organ donor in Cell study; individual animal in independent counter-context studies

evidence: Newly located author dataset is DOI10.17632/n7jbyznw8g.1 and describes NMR/MS data. Its metadata was inspected; spectra/files and donor-level physiology were not.

Independent 2024 APAP work found UAMC-3203 protection associated with Sab/pJNK effects despite little lipid peroxidation. Drug benefit alone therefore cannot identify ferroptosis as the causal injury mechanism.
A randomized rat study beginning treatment 3 days after stroke found mixed cognitive outcomes, including worse aversive learning.
limitations: APAP and repeated systemic post-stroke exposure do not demonstrate toxicity or failure of brief ex vivo lung dosing. They limit broad mechanism/safety claims.
Cell full organ methods remain unrecovered. Human dose, exact salt, effect magnitude and washout cannot be filled from secondary accounts.
FXT-002/003 PK/safety findings cannot be assigned to FXT-001.
existing_candidate_updates.verdict: RETAIN_SECONDARY_COMPARATOR; no S-tier or broad safety promotion.
existing_candidate_updates.decisive_next_proof: Specify the exact material and quantify recipient carryover. In a function-led comparison, use orthogonal lipid-peroxidation/death evidence and avoid treating reduced oxidation alone as organ recovery.
existing_candidate_updates.go_rule: Proceed to differentiated preservation proof if organ function persists under drug-free reperfusion and exposure is reproducible.
existing_candidate_updates.stop_rule: Stop a duplicate business thesis or broad repair claim if it only repeats the existing preservation result, or if functional benefit vanishes after withdrawal.
existing_candidate_updates.material_route: Public free-base and HCl research listings; author analytical-data metadata improves traceability but is not authenticated physical material.
existing_candidate_updates.model_readiness: Published organ setting exists; a qualified local circuit, donor supply and exact protocol remain to be established.
existing_candidate_updates.rights_and_program: Current science-park listing still identifies FiriX as developer of FXT-001; no abandoned-asset inference.

new_candidate_screens.name: Sivelestat as a donor-lung protease comparator
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: Sivelestat sodium tetrahydrate, ONO-5046; use active-moiety equivalents when comparing preparations.

independent_unit.unit: rat graft/recipient; patient for systemic trials

evidence: Donor flush before 16h cold storage improved 48h transplanted-rat oxygenation; high-dose and control values were about379 versus134mmHg.
Pig EVLP abstract supports NE inhibition through four-hour recipient reperfusion, but exact inhibitor identity was not resolved in its retrieved text.
Systemic STRIVE lacked primary benefit and had a late mortality signal; 2026 cardiac-surgery study reported less ARDS in a different perioperative setting.
limitations: Neither human clinical population establishes ex vivo-only efficacy.
A simple NE inhibitor is not a substitute for demonstrated dual NE/PR3 inhibition.
No treated-human-donor-lung study was verified.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: ACTIVE_COMPARATOR; not a standalone top-priority promotion.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: Compare matched NE suppression with AAT in a clinically relevant protein milieu, then test persistent graft function and residual recipient exposure.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: A simpler product is justified only by equivalent-or-better useful function with a measurable handling/exposure advantage.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Stop if benefit requires prolonged systemic exposure, disappears after washout, or offers no advantage over optimized AAT/perfusion.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: Public identity and manufactured-drug precedent; the rat paper specifies sodium tetrahydrate. Current stock, specific commercial lot and perfusate qualification not established.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published rat/pig transplant models; qualified local models and human organ supply not established.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: Old, extensively developed compound and known graft-use literature; no novelty/FTO claim.

new_candidate_screens.name: Bis-T-23 for selected proteinuric podocytopathy
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: Bis-T-23/Ryngo1-23/AG1717, CAS171674-76-3; exact E/E chemical identity must be reconciled across supplier metadata.

independent_unit.unit: individual rodent; glomeruli and cells are nested

evidence: Treatment began 12 days after PAN injury when proteinuria was high; six daily treatments reduced proteinuria at days18 and24.
Genetic ACTN4 and other models support a post-deficit cytoskeletal strategy; later multi-nephron work supplies related rather than fully independent corroboration.
Independent 2025 NOS1AP-null mice did not reduce albuminuria, including early postdose sampling.
limitations: The effect is genotype/context dependent; it is not universal repair of monogenic proteinuria.
No human therapeutic exposure or durable human filtration-barrier rescue was verified.
Dynamin-mediated trafficking and other cellular functions may be affected; public catalog also describes endocytosis inhibition.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: RESEARCH_RESERVE; strongest new kidney proof candidate in this workstream, below current leaders.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: Use independently built, mutation-defined human podocyte barrier models with established leakage. Compare genuine albumin selectivity and survival with existing supportive therapy, track free exposure and preserve endocytosis.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: Advance if post-deficit barrier repair reproduces across responsive genotypes and independent lots within a functional safety window.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Stop broad CKD/genetic-disease claims if benefit is absent in human functional models or achievable exposure perturbs essential trafficking.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: Abcam AB146050 and other public chemical listings; a public dynamin-stabilizer patent discloses material. No received lot or stock verified. Supplier textual structure fields should not replace LC-MS/NMR identity.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published rodent models and public engineered-cell approach; patient-specific mature filtration model still a development task.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: US8809386B2 displays active on the retrieved patent page; neither old publication nor catalog access implies commercial clearance.

new_candidate_screens.name: Emricasan for injured donor-liver NMP
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: Emricasan/IDN-6556/PF-03491390, irreversible pan-caspase inhibitor; published liver study used MCE material in DMSO.

independent_unit.unit: individual donor liver; serial biopsies not independent

evidence: Five consecutive discarded human livers received emricasan before NMP; four met hepatocellular viability criteria, while one did not. Eleven controls were historical and stratified by outcome.
Caspase/cytokine suppression was clear; liver investigators explicitly did not establish definitive functional rehabilitation. Bile production did not differ.
An earlier99-patient randomized preservation trial provides human exposure precedent, with organ-only and organ-plus-recipient regimens; it is not the NMP cohort.
limitations: Historical/outcome-stratified controls cannot establish a four-of-five causal rescue rate.
Injured cholangiocyte function and recipient durability remain unproven for the proposed NMP product.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: HOLD_FOR_FUNCTIONAL_CAUSALITY; useful comparator, not leading asset.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: A contemporaneous donor-balanced comparison must demonstrate improved hepatocellular and biliary function after a defined injury and drug-free reperfusion, beyond caspase inhibition.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: Advance only on clinically useful functional recovery and retained bile-duct integrity at reproducible exposure.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Stop if only inflammatory/apoptosis biomarkers change, function mirrors historical selection, or cell-death suppression masks nonviable tissue.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: Exact published research supplier/formulation route exists; no lot qualification or clinical supply established.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published human NMP implementation and public GEO datasets; local organ access unverified. Transcriptomic reanalysis cannot establish treatment randomization.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: US20240268372A1 displays pending and specifically addresses caspase inhibition in organ preservation; no FTO conclusion.

new_candidate_screens.name: RTR tripeptide for lung-graft reperfusion injury
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: L-arginine–threonine–arginine (RTR), PGP-neutralizing tripeptide; terminal chemistry, counterion, purity and activity must be fixed for a new lot.

independent_unit.unit: individual transplanted mouse; human BAL donor for observational associations
independent_unit.count_boundary: Human cohorts assess target association, not treatment. Tissue fields do not increase mouse N.

evidence: 2026 primary study gave recipient-IV RTR immediately before reperfusion after18h cold ischemia; oxygenation/compliance improved at4h, with four mice per main functional group.
Human BAL target associations and syngeneic replication within the same study support biology, not independent therapeutic efficacy.
limitations: Ex vivo-only administration is a new route hypothesis.
No delayed established-PGD rescue, durable graft survival, human treatment, exposure window or active comparator was demonstrated.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: EARLY_RESERVE; public short-peptide build route, insufficient translational validation.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: Independently verify peptide identity/PGP neutralization and distinguish sequence-specific activity from charge effects. Establish whether an ex vivo pulse retains functional benefit under recipient-like reperfusion versus AAT/sivelestat.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: Advance only if a defined local route yields useful persistent graft function with a measured exposure margin.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Stop if only recipient systemic predosing works, a matched control peptide reproduces the benefit, or effects are limited to short-term markers.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: Public three-residue sequence makes independent synthesis plausible; exact published finished material not fully reconciled and no lot or stock claimed.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published murine transplantation model; human donor intervention and local access remain unverified.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: Current claim-specific commercial mapping not completed; short public sequence does not establish unencumbered use.

new_candidate_screens.name: QX77/CA77 for cystinosis tubular transport
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: QX77/CA77, CAS1798331-92-6; not the distinct analogue CA77.1.

independent_unit.unit: engineered HK-2 CTNS-null line and independent culture experiments

evidence: At20µM nominal exposure for48–72h, engineered CTNS-null HK-2 cells improved Rab11 trafficking and megalin localization.
2024 work found QX77/CA77 increased Rab11-FIP4; broader genetic Rab11-FIP4 rescue findings cannot all be attributed to the small molecule.
limitations: Membrane receptor localization is not measured whole-tubule solute/protein recovery.
Cell counts are not independent patients; no therapeutic human kidney exposure or in-vivo Fanconi rescue was established.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: DISCOVERY_HOLD; functional transport and exposure must precede promotion.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: In independent CTNS-deficient polarized human proximal tubules, require improved receptor-mediated uptake and vectorial transport, including a cysteamine background, across a measured free-exposure range.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: Advance if transport improvement exceeds cysteamine alone without losing polarity or viability and reproduces in donor-derived disease material.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Stop if only localization/vesicle-motion markers improve or functional concentration exceeds the tolerable exposure window.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: MCE HY-112483 public exact identity and catalog; lot/stock unverified. Independent reconstruction requires identity and potency assays.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published CRISPR HK-2 approach provides a rebuild route, not a ready patient-derived transport model; no exact deposited clone assumed.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: No claim-specific clearance or current clinical efficacy established in this bounded search.

new_candidate_screens.name: Genistein for cystinosis renal progression
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: Genistein, defined flavonoid; the mouse study used a specified dietary product, not an unspecified nutraceutical mix.

independent_unit.unit: individual female mouse; repeated urinary samples nested

evidence: Two-to16-month treatment preserved architecture and improved relative creatinine clearance (median0.62 versus0.44 untreated; WT normalized1).

Urinary Fanconi measures did not improve significantly; cysteamine comparator performed better on several tubular parameters. This was early prolonged treatment rather than reversal of an established deficit.
limitations: A glomerular progression signal does not establish proximal-tubular functional restoration.
Add-on benefit with cysteamine was not established; the comparison was separate treatment arms.
High mouse dietary exposure and reproductive/endocrine effects require a translational window.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: DEPRIORITIZE_FANCONI_RESCUE_THESIS; progression-adjunct hypothesis remains distinct and unproven.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: Only reopen with added transport/function over cysteamine in an established-deficit human model at plausible free exposure.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: Require additive clinically relevant function, not lower lysosomal staining alone.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Stop the present rescue thesis if tubular losses remain unchanged or benefit requires preventive high-dose exposure.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: Public exact chemical and published commercial dietary source; finished formulation/lot and achievable kidney exposure not qualified.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published Ctns-null mouse study; a suitable human transport assay needs qualification.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: No independent differentiated product, exclusivity or commercial-rights conclusion established.

new_candidate_screens.name: Luteolin for cystinosis Fanconi dysfunction
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: Luteolin, defined flavonoid (not genistein); published dietary exposure differs from the earlier50µM cellular screen.
evidence: Earlier cellular/zebrafish results suggested improved endocytosis and lysosomal biology.

Six-month mouse treatment at150mg/kg/day improved selected cellular markers but did not improve Fanconi dysfunction or renal inflammation. Filtration remained normal during observation, so that study cannot test rescue of impaired GFR.
limitations: The tested mechanism-marker effects did not translate to the intended tubular function.
A new exposure or formulation strategy would be a new hypothesis, not validation of the original result.
new_candidate_screens.verdict: STOP_CURRENT_FANCONI_PRODUCT_THESIS; retain as an informative negative comparator.
new_candidate_screens.decisive_next_proof: No further same-regimen promotion. Reopen only after a specific changed article/exposure produces independent post-deficit functional transport benefit.
new_candidate_screens.go_rule: A redesigned intervention must demonstrate function beyond the prior negative study.
new_candidate_screens.stop_rule: Do not progress based on repeated p62/LAMP1/apoptosis marker normalization.
new_candidate_screens.material_route: Published commercial reagent route and defined chemical; ease of acquisition does not repair the functional evidence.
new_candidate_screens.model_readiness: Published mouse and cellular models; no treatment effect on the required physiological endpoint established.
new_candidate_screens.rights_and_program: No new differentiated asset or commercial-rights determination.

retrieval_limits: Large FXT Cell author PDF was not retried. Public publisher access did not expose full organ methods; author data-deposit metadata is not donor-level physiology.
AAT2018 full direct PMC page hit a browser-check response; primary abstract, indexed methods/results and captions were inspected. Arm-level N is not invented.
Pig NE-inhibitor abstract omits exact drug name; it is class support rather than transferred sivelestat evidence.
process_lessons: Screen positive cellular findings together with their long-term functional follow-up: luteolin and genistein show why mechanistic normalization cannot substitute for the selected organ task.
Negative independent context data should bound a candidate, not be erased or generalized to every context: NOS1AP limits Bis-T-23; systemic STRIVE is not an ex vivo sivelestat trial.
A mechanistic comparator can increase the information value of a leader experiment even when it is not a new standalone venture.
A verified sequence/chemical identity, a catalog listing, physical stock, authenticated lot, model access and commercial rights remain separate facts.
